paper_title: VisuoThink Empowering LVLM Reasoning with Multimodal Tree Search
caption: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (right) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with both GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates how Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) varies with the rollout-search tree width (number of child nodes), showing two model curves. The x-axis is labeled “Num. of Child Nodes (Tree Width)” on a linear scale with values shown at 1, 3, 5, and 7 (tick interval 2). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy@1 (%)” on a linear scale, spanning roughly from 15 to the high 30s, with labeled ticks at 15, 20, 25, 30, and 35 (interval 5 percentage points). One line corresponds to GPT-4o, drawn in darker blue with a solid line and filled circular markers; it increases from 24.4% at tree width 1 to 28.9% at 3 and 34.4% at 5, then decreases to 31.1% at 7. The other line corresponds to Claude-3.5-Sonnet, drawn in a lighter blue with a solid line and “x” markers; it moves from 26.7% at tree width 1 to 27.8% at 3, then declines to 24.4% at 5 and further to 20.0% at 7.
